description: Staff updated on immigration, diversity, and accessibility initiatives.

chips.text: Received as information
Director to present on backlash against Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion initiatives.
Accessibility survey seeks input from people with disabilities and caregivers.
Saskatoon has a unique city-funded immigration diversity consultant position.
No update provided on the Naming Committee's legacy work.
Internship program supports newcomers, racialized, and Indigenous communities.

segments.title: Immigration Diversity Inclusion Consultant Introduction
description: Position originated from a 2004-05 committee request for immigration study.
City made the position permanent and full-time in 2015.
Role involves internal and external community development and connections.
Works to ensure services and communications are accessible to everyone.

chips.text: Position connects with newcomer and refugee communities for public engagement.
Saskatoon's city-funded position is unique among most municipalities nationally.
April offers to provide a plain language lens for committee work.
Newcomers and refugees are supported in accessing city services.

segments.title: Organization Development Consultant Introduction
description: Position focuses on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) within the city.
Works with internal departments and external agencies on DEI initiatives.
Supports incorporating DEI into collective agreements and union discussions.
Facilitates monthly DEI committees across various city units.

chips.text: Position supports DEI within the city's unionized workplaces and workforce.
Saskatoon is a leader in creating DEI committees within unionized workplaces.
City staff, union members, and youth are impacted by DEI initiatives.

segments.title: EDI Backlash and Future Discussion
description: Striker, an adjunct professor, will present on the state of EDI next week.
Presentation titled "EDI Dead?" aims to spark conversation on current challenges.
Discusses backlash against EDI, including a US government list of banned words.
Session will explore how EDI needs to evolve and move forward.

chips.text: Striker notes a US government list of banned words including "black," "women," and "EDI."
The upcoming presentation has garnered significant public interest with 600 attendees.

segments.title: Accessible Saskatchewan Act Compliance Survey
description: City is conducting an accessibility survey to comply with new provincial act.
Survey seeks feedback on accessibility barriers from residents and employees.
Consultation included an expert and community members to develop the survey.
Report on barriers and city's three-year plan due by December 3, 2025.

chips.text: Survey targets people with disabilities, older adults, caregivers, and service providers.
The survey is currently live and open for feedback.
City will hold focus groups and reach out to under-represented groups.
Saskatoon is ahead of other cities in preparing for the Accessible Saskatchewan Act.
